articles.title: In 1849, Henry Box Brown escaped slavery by having himself nailed inside a wooden box about 3 feet long and shipped from Richmond to Philadelphia, a 27-hour journey that at one point left him upside down
articles.summary: A wooden box became Henry Box Brown's route to freedom in 1849.
articles.body: A wooden box became Henry Box Brown's route to freedom in 1849. With little room to move and only a few openings for air, he agreed to be transported as a parcel from Richmond, Virginia, to Philadelphia. The journey lasted more than a day and involved several changes of transport. At one point, the container was left upside down for hours.Brown survived the dangerous journey and emerged in Philadelphia, where members of an anti-slavery organisation received him. His escape became one of the most unusual accounts of resistance to slavery in 19th-century America.According to the informationa available on National Park Service's webiste, Brown arranged the journey with the help of two men, James Caesar Anthony Smith and Samuel Alexander Smith. They organised a wooden container measuring approximately 3 feet in length, 2.5 feet in depth and 2 feet in width. Three openings provided ventilation. Brown also took water and a tool that could be used to make more holes.On the day of his escape, Brown climbed inside. His helpers secured the container with nails before sending it out of Richmond. It travelled by different means, including rail, wagon and steamboat, before reaching Philadelphia.The instructions on the package indicated that it should remain upright. However, those handling it did not always follow them. The box was overturned twice during the journey. On one occasion, Brown remained head down for a prolonged period, and the position put his life at risk. A stretch of the journey continued in this position for 18 miles.When the package finally reached Philadelphia, abolitionists from the Pennsylvania Anti-Slavery Society took charge of it. They opened the box with concern about what they might find inside. Brown was alive.The family separation that led to his escapeBorn into slavery in Virginia in 1815 or 1816, he was sent to Richmond to work in a tobacco factory after the death of the man who enslaved his family.He married Nancy around 1836. She was enslaved by a different owner. The couple had three children and were expecting another when Nancy and the children were sold in August 1848. They were taken to North Carolina, leaving Brown in Richmond.He spent several months dealing with the separation before deciding to escape. His first challenge was finding people who could help him. Through James Caesar Anthony Smith, a free Black man from his church choir, he made contact with Samuel Alexander Smith, a shoemaker who agreed to assist him for money.They considered other possibilities before choosing the box as their means of transport. Samuel Smith also contacted James Miller McKim, a Philadelphia abolitionist involved in helping enslaved people escape.From an escapee to an anti-slavery campaignerBrown's arrival in Philadelphia marked the beginning of a different chapter. He soon became involved in the abolitionist movement and began speaking publicly about slavery and his escape.In May 1849, he addressed the New England Anti-Slavery Convention in Boston. His story attracted attention among campaigners, and he became known by the name Henry Box Brown.He later worked with Charles Stearns on a book recounting his escape. Published in Boston in September 1849, it helped take his experience to a wider audience. Brown travelled across parts of New England, selling the book and speaking at anti-slavery gatherings.He also took his story to the stage. In 1850, he began presenting a moving panorama called Henry Box Brown's Mirror of Slavery. The production used a series of changing images to depict slavery and his escape.Brown left for England in October 1850 with Samuel Smith. The move came amid fears that the Fugitive Slave Bill could put him at risk of being captured and returned to Virginia. His working relationship with Smith eventually broke down over financial disagreements.Brown remained in England for several years, moving away from anti-slavery lectures and into entertainment. He presented shows, adopted the stage persona of an African prince and later performed as a mesmerist.He returned to the United States in 1875 with his wife and daughter. His performances included appearances in which he climbed into the same box associated with his escape. Brown later settled in Toronto, Canada, where he died on June 15, 1897.You use AI every day. articles.title: At least 31 killed in fuel tanker fire near Cairo, Egypt’s Health Ministry says
articles.summary: A tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed in Egypt’s Giza governorate Wednesday, igniting a massive fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population.
articles.body: A tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed in Egypt’s Giza governorate Wednesday, igniting a massive fire that killed at least 31 people and injured 21 others, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population. The fire broke out above Tunnel 10 in the Warraq district of Imbaba, near Cairo’s Ring Road, the ministry said. Thirty-nine ambulances were deployed to the scene, and the injured were taken to three hospitals, according to the ministry. Health Minister Khaled Abdelghaffar raised the state of readiness at hospitals near the site and traveled to the scene and referral hospitals to monitor the response, the ministry said. Egypt’s Petroleum Ministry said earlier that the privately operated tanker veered off the road and crashed before exploding. The Egyptian Red Crescent said it also deployed emergency response teams to the scene and to the hospital to support Civil Defense, ambulance crews and other authorities responding to the fire. Video published by the Al Arabiya Egypt news outlet showed a large blaze engulfing vehicles on the road near Cairo, with thick plumes of black smoke rising above the area. The Health Ministry said authorities were continuing to monitor the incident and provide medical care to those injured. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Urgent advisory warns Thanksgiving drivers of severe gridlock, lockouts and tire traps
articles.summary: Millions of Americans are hitting the road for Thanksgiving. AAA predicts 81.5 million travelers, warning of dead batteries, flat tires and lockouts.
articles.body: Drivers hitting the road for Thanksgiving face an urgent warning from AAA as 72.9 million motorists prepare for severe gridlock across the nation’s highways during peak travel hours. A Nov. 16 AAA release noted that 81.5 million Americans are projected to travel at least 50 miles from home between Tuesday and Monday — with nearly 90% opting to drive. That surge comes with risks, the AAA says. The auto club is cautioning travelers to brace for dead batteries, lockouts, rental car headaches, the commonly overlooked "door jamb" tire trap and roadwork "ghost zones" that could trick drivers. WORST AIRPORTS FOR THANKSGIVING TRAVEL CHAOS RANKED AS MAJOR US HUBS TOP LIST With highways at capacity and roadside assistance stretched thin, a preventable breakdown can quickly derail holiday plans. AAA is urging every driver to run through a critical pre-trip checklist to avoid getting stranded. Last Thanksgiving, AAA responded to more than 562,000 emergency roadside calls. Here are five topic areas to consider before hitting the road. 1. Holiday traffic peaks Holiday travelers mixing with afternoon commuters will create heavy bottlenecks, and major metro areas are expected to bear the brunt. New York; Washington, D.C.; Los Angeles; and Boston are projected to see more than double their normal congestion, according to AAA and transportation data provider INRIX. HOLIDAY AIRFARE HITS 10-YEAR HIGH AS THANKSGIVING AND CHRISTMAS TRAVEL COSTS SOAR The worst window to drive Wednesday is between noon and 7 p.m., while Sunday return traffic peaks from noon to 8 p.m., according to AAA. "Drivers should consider hitting the road in the morning to avoid the heaviest congestion," the AAA release says. 2. Batteries, lockouts and rental cars Thanksgiving often arrives right as the first real frost sets in. Freezing temperatures are tough on cars. Cold weather dramatically reduces a car battery's ability to hold a charge, according to AAA. When temperatures drop, dead batteries quickly turn into AAA's top roadside rescue call, the organization said in a January release. NEW YORK AND LA DIDN'T WIN AMERICA'S BEST MEGA AIRPORT TITLE, BUT ONE MIDWEST HUB DID Distracted holiday packing also leads to a spike in keys locked in the trunk. "Check the basics before you leave and don't ignore warning signs that something may be wrong," AAA spokesperson Montrae Waiters said in a statement. 3. 'Door jamb' tire trap Cold November temperatures cause tire pressure to drop, sending plenty of Thanksgiving drivers to gas station air pumps before a long trip. AAA warns against filling tires to the maximum PSI stamped on the rubber sidewall, which can hurt handling and traction. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "Do not use the pressure molded into the tire sidewall, as it indicates the pressure needed to meet the tire's full-rated load-carrying capacity," AAA said in a maintenance guide. "It is not the ideal tire pressure specified for your vehicle." 4. 'Ghost' work zones State DOTs pause active roadwork and send crews home for Thanksgiving, which can trick drivers into treating construction zones like open highways. AAA's Club Alliance encourages drivers to minimize distractions, check their speed and to always read the signs. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Work zones sometimes cause congestion, delays and traffic queues," AAA says. "Be alert and watch for sudden stops. "Signs provide guidance to road users of traffic laws or regulations within the work zones. Remember that signs, cones, barrels and flaggers are there to help you drive safely through the work zone." 5. Pre-trip safety checklist Check your tires and spare: Inspect tread, damage and air pressure — including the spare — before hitting the road. Test an aging battery: Have your battery checked if it is more than three years old or the engine has been slow to start. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Pack an emergency kit: Keep water, snacks, a flashlight, first-aid supplies and a phone charger within reach, as well as reflective warning devices and warm clothing. Know what to do if you break down: Pull as far off the road as safely possible and stay in a safe location while waiting for roadside help. articles.body: For a Michigan doctor, a business trip turned expensive when he opted to catch a flight rather than show up to a mandatory divorce hearing, resulting in a default judgment in his 19-year marriage. But while the missed hearing meant he could not overturn the default, the financial and child custody arrangements made in his absence have now encountered a separate setback. The Michigan Court of Appeals upheld the default, but remanded several provisions of the divorce judgment for further proceedings.Marcus Ma and Paula Clare Ma's divorce judgment was partially affirmed and partially vacated in an unpublished opinion dated November 20, 2026, due to insufficient evidence and factual findings on important family law issues.Not showing up for a hearing leads to a default judgmentPaula Ma filed for divorce after 19 years of marriage, the Michigan Court of Appeals says. Her husband, a doctor who traveled for work, missed a mediation and pretrial conference in May 2025, resulting in a default against him. The parties then agreed to set aside that default.But the issue came up again when Marcus did not appear for another pretrial conference scheduled for Feb. 27, 2026. That date had been set at an earlier hearing, and the trial court had specifically ordered both spouses and their attorneys to appear in person.Marcus, who had been reminded several times by the court and his own attorney, asked for an adjournment just before the hearing, citing a work assignment. The request was refused. On the morning of the conference, he told court staff that he was boarding a plane and would not be attending the conference.The trial court entered another default, and then entered a judgment of divorce. Marcus appealed the decision, claiming that his professional obligations were excusable neglect.Appeals court affirms the defaultThe Michigan Court of Appeals saw no reason to overturn the default, noting Marcus had known the hearing requirements and had been through a similar default before.The court found that his decision to prioritize the work trip, despite being expressly told to attend, was not a reasonable excuse. It also noted that he had himself accepted the scheduled date of hearing and was told that his request for postponement would not be entertained. The appellate judges therefore affirmed the lower court's denial of the motion to vacate the default.Lack of financial evidence weakens support ordersBut the default stood, and the Michigan Court of Appeals found serious problems with the financial provisions of the divorce judgment.The lower court had ordered Marcus to pay spousal support for 10 years and fixed child support without hearing evidence of either parent's income. Nor did it provide the factual findings necessary to explain how the amounts were arrived at.The appellate court was unable to determine if the spousal support award was reasonable or if the child support calculation followed the Michigan Child Support Formula.It also held that the spousal support provision could not be made nonmodifiable without a showing that the parties had waived their statutory right to seek modifications.Review of child custody arrangements returnedThe court also struck down provisions related to custody, parenting time and the school district of the children. The Michigan Court of Appeals said the trial court had not properly evaluated the best interests of the couple’s four minor children or determined whether a custodial environment had been established.The case has been sent back to the lower court for further proceedings on spousal support, child support and custody, including whether the children should remain in their current school district.The decision maintains the status quo but directs the lower court to develop a sufficient evidentiary basis before concluding the other divorce terms.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.summary: Blueface has shared his thoughts on N3ON's recent Hawaii collaboration with Nevaeh Akira, the mother of his son.
articles.body: Blueface has shared his thoughts on N3ON's recent Hawaii collaboration with Nevaeh Akira, the mother of his son. During an IRL stream with DeShae Frost, the rapper said N3ON was wrong to get involved with Nevaeh but admitted that he had approved their collaboration earlier. He also explained why he believed the decision could damage his connection with the Kick streamer. His comments come after his public breakup with Nevaeh in September and their later appearance together on a livestream in October, which led to questions about their relationship.Blueface Explains Why He Thinks N3ON Was Wrong to Collaborate With Nevaeh AkiraThe discussion took place during an IRL livestream featuring Blueface and fellow Kick streamer DeShae Frost. The two spoke about N3ON's recent trip to Hawaii with Nevaeh, where the pair spent time together while streaming their activities.N3ON, whose real name is Rangesh, arranged a two-day collaboration with Nevaeh. Their Hawaii streams included several outings, including a picnic near the ocean. Clips from the trip showed flowers, leis and drinks placed around a setup carrying the words "NEON X NEVAEH HAWAII."Blueface was not pleased with the way the collaboration looked. Speaking to Frost, he said:"Imma tell you, bro, that s*** don't look straight."Frost then asked whether he believed N3ON was completely wrong for working with Nevaeh. Blueface agreed but made it clear that he also had something to say about her role in the situation."He is absolutely wrong... But I still approve it, 'cuz the b**** is interested."The rapper then explained that N3ON had asked him about the collaboration before it happened. According to Blueface, he had told the streamer that it was a great idea and had also received Nevaeh's agreement.He added that he was not angry with either of them. However, he felt that Nevaeh's interest in the collaboration also mattered when looking at the situation.The rapper's comments also came with an important distinction. He had initially agreed to the two working together, but he appeared less comfortable with how things developed after that.Blueface Says N3ON's Collaboration With Nevaeh Akira Is Not Worth the RiskBlueface later explained why he had concerns about the Hawaii trip despite giving the collaboration his approval."On a moral standpoint, I don't think it's worth the risk… if me and him got a connection, I don't think that collabing with my [baby momma] is worth..."Frost then finished his thought by saying, "Breaking that up."Blueface's point was that his connection with N3ON could suffer because of the collaboration. He did not say that he wanted to end their friendship, but he questioned whether spending time with his son's mother was worth putting that relationship at risk.There is also some history between Blueface and Nevaeh that helps explain the situation. The two welcomed their son in August 2026. However, on September 8, Blueface announced their breakup during a Kick livestream. Nevaeh later confirmed that they were no longer together. TMZ reported the split following the livestream.The two appeared together again on October 26, when Blueface held their son during another livestream. However, Nevaeh denied that they were officially back together, according to XXL.That distinction matters because Blueface's latest comments do not confirm that the pair have resumed their relationship. Instead, he focused on N3ON's decision to work with Nevaeh and the possible effect it could have on his friendship with the streamer.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Parents of 5-year-old boy killed in Oregon school shooting seek court order against teen gunman's mother
articles.summary: Parents of 5-year-old Rhoam Summer asked an Oregon court to force the shooter's mother to release shotgun records and preserve his online activity.
articles.body: The parents of a 5-year-old boy killed in last month's shooting at an Oregon elementary school are asking a judge to compel the teenage gunman's mother to turn over records detailing how she acquired the shotgun used in the attack and to preserve his online activity before potential evidence disappears. Lillian and Kelik Summer, the parents of kindergartner Rhoam Summer, filed the pre-suit discovery petition Monday in Deschutes County Circuit Court against Shauntai Nickerson, the mother of 16-year-old shooter Griffin J. John II. The filing comes ahead of a planned wrongful death lawsuit over the Oct. 15 rampage at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, where John fatally shot three children and a teacher inside a special education classroom before being killed by an armed parent. Rhoam, who had been in kindergarten for six weeks, is cited in the petition as the youngest person ever killed in a deliberate mass school shooting in the U.S. HERO DAD WHO TOOK DOWN OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER IDENTIFIED ALONG WITH TEACHER, STUDENT BOTH KILLED IN ATTACK Tim Williams, an attorney representing the Summers, told Fox News Digital that law enforcement informed the family it is reviewing "thousands of pages of communication" involving John and "the underbelly of society," which investigators described as "fans of school and mass shootings." Williams said police also indicated that at least one person who communicated with John has been contacted by investigators and "intimated" that one or more artificial intelligence platforms may have been used in planning the attack. "Because criminal liability is much more narrowly focused than civil liability, we are concerned that, without such letters, some of the evidence may not have been gathered by law enforcement, and thus will be lost to time and processes," Williams said, explaining the petition seeks to identify potential defendants so preservation notices can be sent immediately. 911 CALL CAPTURES HERO DAD’S BRAVERY BEFORE HE TOOK DOWN OREGON ELEMENTARY SCHOOL GUNMAN Citing public reports that Nickerson bought a Maverick 88 12-gauge shotgun around her son's birthday in August and gave it to him as a gift, the petition seeks a limited deposition, firearm purchase records, gun-related communications and access to John's social media, gaming and AI accounts. The filing also notes John had not attended school since Nov. 25, 2025, and lists his estate, Bend-La Pine Schools, the unidentified gun seller and any online platforms or users who assisted him as potential defendants. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Nickerson's attorney, David Glenn, told the Summers' lawyers she will not voluntarily produce the records, according to the filing. Fox News Digital reached out to Bend-La Pine Schools for comment and did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: US Education Department probes Virginia schools after sexual abuse scandal
articles.summary: Virginia schools face scrutiny after revelations of abuse and widespread failures in mandatory staff background checks.
articles.body:
The United States Department of Education says it is launching an investigation and withholding funding from a district in the state of Virginia after local officials shut down all of its schools in the wake of a child sexual abuse scandal involving its employees.

“Parents should never have to question whether their child’s school is aiding and abetting child predators,” US Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said in a statement on Tuesday. “The Trump Administration is taking decisive enforcement action to hold those responsible accountable and ensure Virginia schools are safe places for children to learn.”

Officials in Albemarle County, Virginia, announced they were closing all 29 schools in the district last week, after learning that more than 500 staff had not been subjected to a routine background screening for a history of child sexual abuse. The school system has about 2,800 employees, and only a fraction of its $284m budget comes from the federal government.

Local officials emphasised that none of the 524 employees is suspected of abuse.

Approximately 14,000 students attend the schools, and parents have scrambled to find childcare, while many who depend on free school meals for their children have had to look for other sources of food.

Bob Beard, a member of the Albemarle school board, told Al Jazeera that families were struggling to deal with the shutdown, but schools would reopen on Monday.

The child abuse allegations have shaken the county and caught the attention of the Trump administration.

A former elementary school teacher was arrested for possession of child sexual abuse material earlier this year, while a counsellor at another school was put on leave and later indicted on 20 counts of sexual crimes involving seven different children, according to the Albemarle County Police Department.

Two county school officials and a school principal were later charged with failure to report child abuse, and the county’s superintendent of schools resigned.

Jason Grant, a spokesman for Albemarle County Public Schools, told Al Jazeera that none of the individuals implicated in those cases was among the 524 employees who were hired without the proper screening required to check for a history of child sexual abuse.

“This was not about having the policies in place, this was about processes that were not followed,” Grant said. He said officials were working with the state to “make sure the processes are in place to make sure this doesn’t happen again.”

Grant said all employees in the district undergo several stages of vetting, including a criminal background check and an attestation that they have no history of child abuse or neglect. Then the school system submits their information to the Virginia Department of Social Services to verify that they are not part of the agency’s abuse and neglect database.

For three years, it appears that vetting procedures were not consistently applied. Putting employees hired over that period on leave to carry out background checks meant schools would not be able to run, so officials decided to close them until next week.

“Those were for every range of employee, from teachers to bus drivers to substitutes and across the division, so we couldn’t get coverage for that amount of people,” Grant said.

All but three of the 524 employees have now been properly vetted, and none had background issues, Grant said, adding that the county will reopen schools on Monday.

The Trump administration has long called for the dismantling of the Department of Education. The US president signed an executive order last year that tried to set that in motion.

The department, which distributes federal funding to states for use in schools, also traditionally investigates whether local officials are complying with civil rights laws banning discrimination against minorities and marginalised groups.

Since returning to office in 2025, the Trump administration has cut more than half of the department’s staff and subjected it to wider changes it says are aimed at rooting out “diversity, equity, and inclusion” (DEI) policies.

articles.title: We tried Laneige’s viral lip mask, moisturizer and more — here’s what’s actually worth buying
articles.summary: Is Laneige worth it? Our editors tested the Lip Sleeping Mask, Water Bank Cream, Cream Skin toner and more for at least a month. Here’s what’s worth buying.
articles.body: Few skin care brands have turned a single product into a phenomenon quite like Laneige. (Quick pronunciation check: It’s “lah-nEH-zh.”) The Korean brand grew in popularity due to its viral Lip Sleeping Mask — the little pink pot you’ve likely seen on a coworker’s desk or in an influencer’s TikTok routine. But Laneige has grown well beyond lip care, with a full slate of skin care built around hydration, barrier support and the dewy “glass skin” look K-beauty is known for. Our NBC Selected editors have tried a range of the brand’s bestsellers; below are our honest thoughts about the social media-beloved brand and whether it’s actually worth buying. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Our honest review of Laneige The below list includes Laneige products that NBC Selected staffers have personally tested and showcase the range of options available from the brand, including lip treatments, moisturizers and more. Best overall If you want to get started with just one product from Laneige, let it be this one. The Lip Sleeping Mask is our standout product of the bunch and earns its popular status: Our testers’ lips were noticeably softer by morning, and one jar lasted me more than six months, making the $24 price easy to justify. The formula has shea butter, murumuru seed butter and coconut oil for moisture and vitamin C to protect your lips. You apply the thick balm generously before bed so it can work overnight. “I first bought this lip mask after it got a ton of hype on TikTok and I have to say, it really is extremely effective,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. ”I keep it on my bedside table and put it on before I go to sleep, when my lips tend to get the most dry. I always wake up with super hydrated lips.” Each jar comes with a small silicone spatula so you don’t have to dip your fingers into the pot, though I personally found the spatula to be too small and easy to lose. It’s available in a long list of scents, from the original Berry to rotating limited editions like this season’s Gingerbread. Laneige also recently released a Bespoke collection, which mixes two flavors in one jar. You can also wear a thin layer during the day as a prep step before lipstick. Best moisturizer This moisturizer has hyaluronic acid, a humectant that helps draw water into the skin, along with ceramides, squalane, peptides and panthenol to support the skin’s moisture barrier. I’ve been using this moisturizer for over a month, and its rich, cushiony texture is one of my favorite things about it. It melts into my skin quickly without feeling heavy or greasy. As someone who is conscious about waste, I like that it comes in a refillable tub, so I can just swap the insert instead of buying a new jar. Keep in mind that it contains fragrance, which may irritate some people with sensitive or reactive skin. Best tinted lip I hate sticky gloss, so I was reluctant to try this serum-gloss hybrid, but I was impressed with how hydrated and glowy it left my lips. The applicator is shaped like a mini donut and has a bit of cushion, so it coats lips evenly in one pass. The tint is sheer and buildable, so it pairs well over a lip liner or on its own for a your-lips-but-better look. The only issue was that it took a few tries for me to figure out the right amount of product to squeeze out. A little goes a long way and the first few times I tried it, I squeezed out too much and was left with a bit of a mess on the applicator. The color is also more of a light tint, so if you are looking for a punch of color, this may not be for you. Best daytime lip balm If the Lip Sleeping Mask is Laneige’s nighttime hero, the Lip Glowy Balm is its daytime counterpart. It comes in a squeezable tube with a slanted tip and has a lighter, glossier texture than the mask, making it easy to reapply throughout the day. Shea and murumuru seed butters moisturize, and each scent — Berry, Gummy Bear, Peach Iced Tea, to name a few — comes with a sheer wash of tint. Vanilla and Mango are the closest to clear, in our experience. “I used to use Vaseline to save my dry lips, but I wanted something with color that hydrated them and felt a bit more special,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. “This lip balm is the perfect combo. It is so hydrating, and the formula isn’t too thick or sticky. It gives my lips the perfect shine without being too heavy.” NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio has used this lip balm for years, and she even gave each of her bridesmaids one on her wedding day. “It gives the perfect pop of shine to any lip look,” she says. It also works as a lip primer before lipstick. Keep in mind it doesn’t have SPF, so pair it with a sunscreen lip balm when you’re spending time outdoors. Best toner Instead of a watery or astringent liquid, this toner has a milky texture that combines a moisturizer and a toner into one. According to the brand, you can use this in place of a traditional moisturizer, though I found it a little too lightweight to give me the full amount of moisture my dry skin needs. It has ceramides and peptides to nourish and support the moisture barrier, along with white leaf tea, which is rich in amino acids, to soothe skin, according to the brand. The formula is also fragrance-free, hypoallergenic and accepted by the National Eczema Association, making it one of the most sensitive skin-friendly options on this list. “I’ve tested hundreds of products as a beauty editor and this toner-moisturizer hybrid is one of my favorite two-fer products ever,” says NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown. “It feels like water in your hands but transforms into a lightweight moisturizer when rubbed into the skin that doesn’t feel greasy. I’ve used it for months at a time in the past and love how much it shortened my skin care routine without harming my skin.” You can pump it into your palms and pat it in after cleansing or buy a spray top to spritz it on your face as a midday pick-me-up, which is exactly what I do. I keep a bottle near my desk and spray it on my face anytime I need a refresh. Best overnight face mask You can use this overnight mask as the last step of your night routine, after moisturizing, then rinse it off in the morning. It has collagen and peptides, which experts told us can help skin look plumper and smoother, along with hyaluronic acid to hydrate as you sleep, according to the brand. Once colder weather hits, my skin gets really dry and needs a boost of moisture. I started using this mask nightly over a month ago and noticed my skin looks and feels so much more hydrated. I also really like the texture: It has a light, almost whipped feel and sinks into my skin quickly. Best under-eye patches These under-eye patches come in a pack of thirty and contain spicules, which experts have previously told us are tiny, needle-like structures that create microchannels in your skin to help beneficial skin care ingredients better permeate. In this case, that means PDRN, niacinamide, caffeine, hyaluronic acid and collagen. “I tried these eye masks when the brand first launched them in September, and I was pleasantly surprised by how hydrating and cooling they felt under my eyes,” says Godio. “I keep them in my fridge and wear them in the morning to depuff and brighten my under-eyes, which helps make me look much more awake before I head out for the day.” Godio also likes that the patches are textured, which helps prevent them from slipping off. As for downsides, she says the serum pills and leaves residue on her skin after she takes them off. She also notes that there is a lot of excess serum left in the packaging, which makes them feel a little too slimy for her liking. What to know before buying Laneige Resoundingly, NBC Selected editors all have positive things to say about Laneige. That said, like with any brand, there are certain things you may want to keep in mind, including: Fragrance is common. The Water Bank Cream, Bouncy & Firm Sleeping Mask and every lip product we tested contain added fragrance, which can be irritating on sensitive skin types. If you have reactive skin, Cream Skin is the most sensitive skin-friendly pick on this list.The products we tested don’t replace sunscreen. The Lip Glowy Balm and Glaze Craze don’t have SPF, and neither does the Water Bank Cream and other moisturizers. Apply a separate broad-spectrum face sunscreen in the morning and use an SPF lip product when you’ll be outdoors.Jar packaging isn’t for everyone. The Water Bank Cream and Bouncy & Firm Sleeping Mask both come in open-mouth jars, so you’re dipping your fingers in each time. If that bothers you, use a clean spatula, or reach for pump- and tube-packaged picks like Cream Skin and the lip balms. How we tested Laneige products Five NBC Selected editors tested a range of Laneige’s bestsellers for at least one month, though testing periods varied by product. Several editors have used the brand’s lip products, like the Lip Sleeping Mask, for years. The products we tested cover several skin care categories, including lip masks, lip balms, toners, serums and moisturizers. We worked products into our existing routines and kept our own skin concerns in mind (including dryness and sensitivity). While testing, we followed the brand’s instructions on how to use each product and focused on the following questions: Texture and application: How does the product feel on skin or lips? Is it easy to spread or apply? Does it feel sticky, heavy or greasy?Effectiveness over time: How did skin and lips feel after weeks of use? Did the product do what it promised, such as hydrating or smoothing? Did it cause any irritation?Ease of use: Does it fit easily into a morning or nighttime routine? Is it clear how much to use and when?Scent: Does it have a noticeable fragrance? If so, is it pleasant, overpowering or irritating?Packaging: Does it come in a pump, tube or jar? Is it easy and hygienic to dispense? Is it travel-friendly?Value: Do the size and results justify the price? Would we repurchase it? Who is Laneige for? Laneige is best known for hydrating lip and skin care, which means it’ll appeal most to people who deal with dryness and compromised moisture barriers, as well as people looking for lightweight and layerable Korean skin care. If hydration isn’t your primary concern, Laneige may not be the best one-brand solution. If you’re focused on acne, discoloration or stronger actives, you may need to supplement your routine with products from other K-beauty brands like Medicube (many of which fall within the same price point). While there is a heavy focus on dry skin, those with oily or combination skin may prefer the Water Bank Gel Moisturizer, which Laneige describes as a lightweight, cooling option. Keep in mind many of the products we tested have fragrance, so people with sensitive skin should check the ingredient lists carefully. The brand’s Cream Skin line, including the toner and sheet mask, is our strongest recommendation for people who want lightweight, fragrance-free hydration that won’t cause irritation (the line is even accepted by the National Eczema Association). Meanwhile, the Water Bank Cream is best for normal-to-dry skin that can tolerate fragrance. In terms of lip care, which we think the brand does best, the Glaze Craze is the better pick for shine and tint, though the Lip Glowy Balm is easier for everyday, on-the-go use. If you’re a fan of Laneige’s viral lip mask but prefer a tube application over a jar, the Lanolips 12 Hour Overnight Lip Mask is worth considering, though it only comes in one flavor (as opposed to the many offered by Laneige). Why trust NBC Selected? I am a commerce editor at NBC Selected and a journalist who regularly covers wellness, beauty, home and lifestyle. I have written about honey skin care, the Jellycat craze and more. I have used Laneige’s Lip Sleeping Mask for years and have tested a number of their other products, too. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Winter rains threaten 1,000 Gaza shelter sites, councils warn
articles.summary: About 200,000 tents need replacing, Gaza’s municipalities say, as the EU urges Israel to reopen all crossings.
articles.body:
Gaza’s municipalities have warned that winter rains could flood about 1,000 camps and other sites hosting displaced Palestinians in the war-torn enclave, adding that damage to drains and sewers, and a shortage of pumps, have left their crews with little means to clear the water.

After a meeting in Gaza City on Wednesday, the Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities singled out al-Mughraqa and al-Zahra in central Gaza, where water levels in Wadi Gaza could rise suddenly. Across the territory, about 200,000 tents need replacing, and more than 2,000 damaged buildings are at risk of collapse, the union said. Gaza’s Government Media Office had warned on Tuesday that it expected another storm within days.

This is Gaza’s fourth winter since Israel launched its war in October 2023. The union said storms in early November flooded about 70,000 tents and affected more than 350,000 displaced people. During a winter storm this November, families piled sand at tent entrances to keep out the rain. Others carried their children out and salvaged what belongings they could.

One displaced mother said she had cut up the burial shroud she had bought for her son and used it to patch her tent. She wanted to keep the family’s bedding and clothes dry. “I couldn’t get a tarpaulin,” she said.

When the first rains hit, Gaza’s civil defence crews reached only a minority of those who called for help. Most of the other callers received advice by phone, Al Jazeera reported .

In Brussels on Wednesday, the European Commission called on Israel to reopen all Gaza crossings to humanitarian aid. Commission spokesperson Eva Hrncirova said tents were waiting on trucks outside Gaza because Israel had not allowed them or the equipment needed to put them up to enter.

The UN said earlier this month that more than 150,000 tents were awaiting entry into Gaza.

Al Jazeera’s open-source unit (Ar.) measured a queue of trucks stretching about 1.1km (0.7 miles) along the Egyptian road to the Rafah crossing in a November 17 satellite image, up from about 460 metres (1,510 feet) on October 6. The images do not establish what the trucks carried. Freight from Egypt is routed through the Karem Abu Salem crossing, known as Kerem Shalom in Israel, for inspection rather than entering Gaza through Rafah.

COGAT, the Israeli military body that coordinates aid, said that nearly 100,000 tents had entered Gaza since the start of a winter aid programme. It said Israel would allow reconstruction equipment into Gaza only after Hamas had fully disarmed.

Inside Gaza, aid workers have cleared drains, installed flood barriers and reinforced shelters. The UN’s humanitarian affairs office reported on November 20 that teams had recorded such work at 162 of the 356 flood-prone locations they had identified. Gaza’s municipalities are asking for pumps, backup generators and fuel before the next storm, as well as 10,000 tonnes of cement for emergency repairs and mobile homes that can withstand wind and rain.

articles.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to weather
articles.summary: Preparations to hold the iconic celebration - known for the massive balloons that float past the city's skyscrapers - had already begun on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday, due to severe weather.

Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers ,had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.

The last time the parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never been postponed due to weather. In 1971 Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture.

The centennial parade's postponement comes as a potent Nor'easter storm is expected to make it too windy for the iconic balloons to fly.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's said, according to US media.

The retailer, citing "expected severe weather", said it is working through operational logistics and will share details when they are finalised.

The parade is expected to kick off at 0830 local time (1330 BST) on Saturday.

The US National Weather Service has issued a high wind warning, valid from 10:00 local time (15:00 GMT) on Thursday until 01:00 (06:00 GMT) on Friday with gusts potentially reaching 60mph (97km/h) - although the very strongest winds are likely to occur after the parade was due to end.

Heavy rain and coastal flooding will pose additional hazards across the eastern USA as the storm sweeps through, while some inland parts could also see snow, BBC Weather reports.

articles.title: Thanksgiving flights booked after key hour face double the risk of major delay
articles.summary: Flights after 9 a.m. are twice as likely to be delayed as early departures, Hopper data shows, as storms threaten Northeast hubs this Thanksgiving holiday.
articles.body: As U.S. airports brace for a brutal Thanksgiving rush, travel analysts are warning passengers about a common scheduling mistake that raises the odds of a disrupted trip: booking a flight after 9 a.m. "Flights departing after 9 a.m. are generally twice as likely to be delayed as those departing between 5 a.m. and 8 a.m.," according to Hopper data. The alert lands at an uneasy moment for American flyers, with 69% now ranking delays and cancellations as their top booking concern, according to a Hopper consumer survey. TSA DETECTS SUSPICIOUS MOVEMENT IN TRAVELER'S SUITCASE DURING SECURITY SCREENING A storm system bringing heavy rain, wind and thunderstorms has already swept across the Gulf Coast and Southeast and is bearing down on major Mid-Atlantic and Northeast hubs through Thanksgiving Day, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Confidence has also been tested by recent technical scares. Travelers were shaken by the Nov. 13 FAA ground stop sparked by telecommunications instability. The ground stop halted departures nationwide, resulting in more than 12,400 cancellations, according to the U.S. Department of Transportation and the FAA. TRAVELERS BUSTED AT AIRPORT WITH OVER 3,000 TARANTULAS HIDDEN AWAY IN THEIR SOCKS An isolated outage also prompted a brief ground stop at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Nov. 24, as Fox News Digital previously reported. How the clock turns against travelers Across U.S. domestic flights from 2023 through 2025, just 11% of departures scheduled before 8 a.m. arrived 15 or more minutes late, according to Bureau of Transportation Statistics data analyzed by DelayGuard. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Because commercial jets typically fly multiple legs a day, a storm or runway bottleneck in one hub can affect later routes. Late-arriving aircraft are responsible for 41% of all U.S. delay minutes, an AirDelay analysis noted. Sunrise departures sidestep that chain reaction. "The aircraft has spent the night at the airport, so there is no late inbound flight to wait for," DelayGuard reported. Morning crews are also just beginning their shifts, so earlier snags on the schedule will not hold up boarding, according to DelayGuard. Passengers whose morning flights are disrupted have far more later departures available to rebook. Evening snags leave fewer options, according to AirDelay and CLEAR. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS In addition, travelers willing to brave a 4 a.m. alarm often score lower fares on a 6 a.m. flight than on a 10 a.m. departure, The Points Guy reported. "Taking a morning flight gives you a greater chance of having a plane and crew ready to go," Gary Leff, a Texas-based travel industry expert and author of the blog "View From The Wing," told Fox News Digital. "There's an opportunity to address maintenance issues overnight. So [there's] a likelihood of starting the day with an aircraft that's ready," Leff continued. "Crew have limits in their duty day. They could run out of allowable time with late flights that get delayed," he added. "Early flights mean starting fresh, and you aren't risking your pilots or flight attendants 'timing out.'" Why the day matters Picking the right day of the week can sway the odds as well. Tuesday consistently ranks as the most punctual day at major U.S. airports, with fewer than 19% of departures arriving late — followed closely by Wednesday, according to Bureau of Transportation Statistics records reviewed by DelayGuard. Sunday sits at the bottom, with a quarter of flights running behind schedule, DelayGuard reported. Leff said delays have a ripple effect. "Delays stack throughout the day. If you're on the third or fourth flight operated by your crew or aircraft that day, there were several opportunities for them to get delayed during the day," Leff said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ During peak holiday windows, timing can protect a traveler's wallet, too. Flying home on Sunday can be the costliest option, with round-trip domestic fares averaging $604 compared with roughly $350 for passengers who wait until Monday or Tuesday, according to Hopper's 2026 Holiday Travel Index. "Early flights mean more recovery options." Aviation officials urge passengers to build extra buffer time into their commute, to stay subscribed to airline alerts and to check real-time airport conditions through the FAA's National Airspace System status portal. "Not only are there more same-day options left on the schedule, but available seats are less likely to have been taken by other passengers that were delayed."

articles.title: Tyler Cameron’s 2027 goal is to be a ‘hot dad’ — here’s what he’s relying on to do exactly that
articles.summary: Tyler Cameron’s 2026 was an HGTV and DWTS whirlwind, now he’s sharing the gifts he’s getting his fiance before the year ends and all the things that’ll help him become a “hot dad” in 2027.
articles.body: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. It seems impossible that Tyler Cameron could have a bigger year than 2026. In the past 12 months, he got engaged, announced that he’s expecting a baby with fiancé Tate Madden and competed on Dancing with the Stars. Plus, his HGTV show Bachelor Mansion Takeover premiered and he became part owner of Tinkr, a brand that sells modern home tools. Yet somehow, 2027 is looking just as huge. His daughter is due in March, he’s planning a wedding, he’s going on tour with Dancing with the Stars and he’s filming a new HGTV show. Before all of that, however, he’s slowing down to celebrate the holidays with his loved ones, something he’s looking forward to more than ever. “I’m not going to lie, I was the biggest Grinch,” says Cameron. “I was never really into the holidays because there was always something happening with my family, and it was a ‘hold my breath’ period for a long time. But Tate has really gotten rid of the Grinch and brought out the best in me, so now I love the holidays and I’m so excited about them.” Cameron’s favorite part of the holidays is decorating, especially his Christmas tree. He and Madden put theirs up on November 1 so they could start putting presents underneath it. One of Cameron’s go-to places to get gifts quickly is Amazon, a retailer he’s currently partnering with to curate collections of his top picks and keep track of ideas for everyone. Below, he shared the top gifts he’s giving and hopes to receive this year while reflecting on a jam-packed year. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Dancing with the Stars was a whirlwind that Cameron says gave him numerous life lessons. The biggest? “It’s about the ability to put yourself out there and be fearless,” he says. “Sometimes I get imposter syndrome, or feel like I don’t fit in or I don’t belong — I go back to being that simple guy from Jupiter [Florida] who builds houses, and I forget that I get to do some really cool stuff. During Dancing with the Stars, it was all about that mantra of ‘you can.’ You can put yourself out there and be great. You can step on stage and mess up and still come back. It was a giant confidence builder and honestly one of the most fulfilling things I’ve ever done.” Because he was competing on DWTS, Cameron couldn’t run the 2026 New York City Marathon, which he’s done a few times. He hopes to race in 2027 and apply what he learned on the show to training. The Garmin Vívoactive Smartwatch will also be something he relies on to track his miles, energy levels, sleep and health metrics like heart rate, so that’s one of the gifts he’d love to receive. “Everyone being happy and healthy is really the top thing on my personal wish list,” says Cameron. “It’s an easy thing to say, but I’ve really dialed in on health lately. I lost 11 pounds during Dancing with the Stars, so I want to continue leaning into that — 2027 is the year of being a hot dad.” Beyond running, Cameron likes to do group workouts. When he takes his training outside, he brings the JBL Boombox with him to play music during sessions. The speaker is a gift he says any audiophile in your life would appreciate, especially if they enjoy being the DJ in their friend group. “Rest is so important — I’m very big on it,” says Cameron. “After workouts I use things like a foam roller, but for sleep, I put on mouth tape and nose strips — I do all that kind of stuff. I also use the Therabody sleep mask.” It blocks light to help him fall and stay asleep, and he can choose from three vibration patterns to enhance his slumber with an eye massage. He’s gifting it to loved ones who could use some R&R. This holiday season is the last one Cameron and Madden will celebrate as a party of two — next year, they’ll be sharing their first Christmas with their daughter. So when it comes to buying his fiancé gifts this holiday season, Cameron’s goal is to make her feel totally taken care of. “She has a baby list that I’ll start shopping from, but I want to get her things for herself and that will help her nest,” he says. “She loves anything from HydroJug, and she’s a big fan of Salt & Stone body washes and deodorants. I’m getting her all those simple things that make her happy so she can focus on herself and get ready for the baby.” Cameron’s background is in home construction — before he was on The Bachelorette, and still to this day, he’s a contractor, as well as a real estate agent. He’s always working on something related to home improvement, like his new HGTV show, Let’s Go Back to Your Place, which he starts filming next week. “The best way to describe it is if Room Raiders and House Hunters had a baby,” says Cameron. “I take a bachelor or bachelorette, and I’m their wingman. We go look at houses and they choose someone to date based on that. They never get to meet them until after they decide on the house. Just imagine if you could go through someone’s house before you go on a date with them — imagine how much you could already know about them.” Cameron and Madden are also part owners of Tinkr, a brand that sells modern home tools. It rolled out in major retailers like Target and Kohl’s this year, and in 2027, the company is growing even more, in addition to launching new products. Cameron says he loves Tinkr’s jump starter and toolbox, while Madden is obsessed with the electric scissors. “They’re a must-have in our house for breaking down boxes,” he says.
